image_spec.headline: Fresh vegetables are on track to cost 6.5% more this year.
image_spec.body: Get a heads-up two days before the spinach turns, while there's still time to cook it.

posts.caption:
Bagged spinach. You buy it with the best intentions, and four days later it's a dark green puddle at the bottom of the crisper drawer. Every fridge has one.

It stings a bit more this year. The USDA's latest Food Price Outlook says fresh vegetables are on track to cost 6.5% more in 2026. 💰

That's why we're building Pantry alerts into StashSmart. You get a heads-up 48 hours before something goes bad, which is usually just enough time to toss it into eggs or a pasta.

Coming soon on iPhone. Which vegetable always gets away from you?

image_spec.headline: Eggs are forecast to cost 29.5% less this year. What are you baking first?
image_spec.body: One word in the comments. Cookies, pie, bread, something else.
image_spec.tip: Check the flour before you buy more.

posts.caption:
Finally, a grocery price going the right way. The USDA expects egg prices to come in 29.5% lower this year than last.

Which, honestly, feels like a sign to start the holiday baking.

So what's first at your house? Cookies, pie, banana bread, the cinnamon rolls someone asks for every December. One word is plenty. 🙌

Quick tip before you head to the store: check the cabinet for flour and vanilla first. That half-used bag in the back still counts.
